meta.titre: Mobile Phone Technology: the SIM card, cells, generations and mobile data
meta.sous_theme: SIM card and IMEI, cellular networks, generations 1G to 5G, mobile data and risks

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A trader in a Yaounde market receives a payment by mobile money, phones a supplier in Douala and photographs her goods for her customers, all on one small device. Behind that device are a network of base stations, a small chip card that proves who she is, and a data bundle that she pays for. The GCE asks for the full name of the card, the generations of mobile networks, the uses of a phone and its risks, so each of these ideas deserves a precise answer.

items: Radio waves can carry sound and data through the air without wires.
A network is a group of devices connected so that they can exchange data.
Data is measured in bytes, and a bit is a single 0 or 1.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### How a mobile network works

A mobile phone sends and receives calls and data as radio waves. The area served is divided into **cells**, and each cell has a **base station** (a mast with antennas). The base stations are linked to the system of the network operator (for example MTN or Orange), which connects calls to other phones and to the Internet. When you travel from one cell to the next during a call, the call is passed to the next base station (**handover**) and goes on without a break.

### The SIM card

SIM stands for **Subscriber Identity Module**. It is a small chip card placed in the phone. It identifies the subscriber to the network and holds the information needed to use the subscription; it can also store a few contacts and messages. It is removable: moving the SIM to another phone moves the subscription and the number, but not the photos, apps and contacts saved in the first phone's own memory. The phone itself (the handset) is identified by its **IMEI** number, normally 15 digits, which can be shown by dialling `*#06#`.

### Generations of mobile networks

| Generation | Main step forward |
|---|---|
| 1G | Analogue voice calls |
| 2G | Digital voice calls and text messages (SMS); GSM, the Global System for Mobile Communications, is a well-known 2G standard |
| 3G | Practical mobile internet and video calls |
| 4G | Much faster mobile data, so streaming video is smooth |
| 5G | Faster still, with very short delays |

SMS means Short Message Service (text only) and MMS means Multimedia Messaging Service (pictures, sound and video).

### Smartphone features and uses

A smartphone adds a touch screen, an operating system (Android or iOS), apps, a camera, a GPS receiver, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and a rechargeable battery to the basic call function. It is used for calls, messages, browsing, navigation, photos, learning and mobile money such as MTN Mobile Money or Orange Money.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks how a phone connects
variantes.contenu_markdown: **Mobile data** uses the network operator's base stations and is paid for with a data bundle. **Wi-Fi** connects the phone to a local network, usually through a router, inside a building. **Bluetooth** joins two devices over a very short distance, for example a phone and a headset. A phone can also share its mobile data with other devices as a hotspot.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must discuss the use of phones
variantes.contenu_markdown: Advantages: communication from anywhere, access to information, mobile money, photos, navigation and learning apps. Disadvantages: distraction and wasted study time, cyberbullying, exposure to scams and harmful content, loss of privacy, theft, cost of airtime and data, and misuse in examinations. Always explain each point in one full sentence.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a calculation gives a file size and a connection speed
variantes.contenu_markdown: One byte is 8 bits, so 1 MB is 8 megabits (Mb). Time in seconds = size in megabits / speed in megabits per second (Mbps). In this course take 1 GB = 1024 MB.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Ngum changes to a new phone but keeps his phone number. He saved all his 40 contacts in the memory of the old phone and none on the SIM card.

(a) State what SIM stands for and what Ngum must move to the new phone to keep his number.

(b) What happens to the 40 contacts when he only moves that item? Suggest one way to keep them.

(c) The new phone works on 4G. State one improvement of 4G over 2G.

etapes.action: Expand the abbreviation and state the role of the card.
etapes.justification: The card identifies the subscriber to the network.
etapes.resultat_markdown: SIM means Subscriber Identity Module. Ngum moves the SIM card to keep the number and subscription.

etapes.action: Find where the contacts are stored.
etapes.justification: Contacts saved in the phone memory stay in the old handset; only data on the SIM travels with the card.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The 40 contacts stay in the old phone and do not appear on the new one.

etapes.action: Name a way to keep them.
etapes.justification: The contacts must be copied before the change.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Copy them to the SIM, or export them to a file or an online account, then import them on the new phone.

etapes.justification: 2G was designed for digital calls and text, 4G for fast mobile data.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 4G gives much faster data, so videos stream smoothly.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) SIM means Subscriber Identity Module; he moves the SIM card. (b) The contacts saved in the phone memory remain in the old phone; he should copy them to the SIM or export them to a file or an online account before the change. (c) 4G gives much faster mobile data, so video can be streamed smoothly.

items.erreur_markdown: Expanding SIM as 'Simple Internet Module', or with any words that do not begin with Subscriber.
items.pourquoi_faux: The abbreviation stands for Subscriber Identity Module, because the card identifies the subscriber.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that the SIM card is the phone's memory card that holds photos and apps.
items.pourquoi_faux: Photos and apps are stored in the phone's own memory or on a separate memory card. The SIM identifies the subscriber.
items.correction_markdown: SIM: identity of the subscriber. Memory card: extra storage.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that the IMEI number identifies the subscriber.
items.pourquoi_faux: The IMEI identifies the handset itself. The SIM identifies the subscriber.
items.correction_markdown: IMEI: the phone. SIM: the subscription.

items.erreur_markdown: Thinking that using Wi-Fi uses up the mobile data bundle.
items.pourquoi_faux: Wi-Fi uses the connection of the router. The bundle is used up by mobile data through the operator's network.
items.correction_markdown: Mobile data consumes the bundle; Wi-Fi uses the router's connection.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that 1G was a digital network.
items.pourquoi_faux: The first generation carried analogue voice calls. Digital networks began with 2G.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Write in full the abbreviations SIM and SMS.
(b) Name the first generation of mobile networks that used digital signals.
(c) Name the number that identifies the handset itself.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) SIM: **Subscriber Identity Module**. SMS: **Short Message Service**.

(b) **2G**.

(c) The **IMEI** number.

items.enonce_markdown: Amina buys a 2 GB data bundle. She has already used 300 MB. A video she wants to download is 40 MB. Take 1 GB = 1024 MB. How many whole videos of that size can she still download?
items.solution_markdown:
Bundle in MB: 2 x 1024 = 2048 MB.

Left: 2048 - 300 = 1748 MB.

Number of videos: 1748 / 40 = 43.7, so only whole videos count: **43 videos** (43 x 40 = 1720 MB, and a 44th would need 1760 MB).

items.enonce_markdown:
A file of 12 MB is downloaded on a 4G connection of 8 Mbps and then, in another place, on a slow connection of 2 Mbps. Take 1 byte = 8 bits.

(a) Calculate the download time on each connection.
(b) How much longer does the slow connection take?
(c) State two disadvantages of allowing students to use phones in class.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) 12 MB = 12 x 8 = 96 megabits.

At 8 Mbps: 96 / 8 = **12 s**. At 2 Mbps: 96 / 2 = **48 s**.

(b) 48 - 12 = **36 s** longer.

(c) Any two, explained: students are distracted from the lesson; phones can be used to cheat or to copy answers; messages and games waste study time; phones can be stolen or damaged in class.

items_markdown: A mobile network is made of cells, each served by a base station; handover keeps a call going when you move between cells.
SIM = Subscriber Identity Module: it identifies the subscriber; the IMEI identifies the handset.
1G analogue voice; 2G digital voice and SMS; 3G practical mobile internet; 4G fast mobile data; 5G faster still.
Mobile data uses the operator's network and a bundle; Wi-Fi uses a router; Bluetooth works over a very short distance.
Download time = size in megabits / speed in Mbps, with 1 byte = 8 bits.
